name: OpenFeature
solves: Provides a vendor-neutral OpenFeature SDK for Node and web so application code evaluates flags through a standard API while providers (LaunchDarkly, Unleash, flagd, and others) remain swappable behind the interface. It is an abstraction layer, not a flag product.
best_for: Platforms that must avoid hard-wiring a single feature-flag vendor into application code
Enterprises standardizing flag evaluation behind OpenFeature providers across services
Teams mid-migration between flag vendors who need a stable application API
Organizations adopting CNCF OpenFeature as a governance requirement
Polyglot estates where OpenFeature is the common evaluation abstraction
skip_when: You need a flag product with an admin UI, targeting, and rollouts — pick LaunchDarkly, Unleash, GrowthBook, Flagsmith, or PostHog, then optionally wrap them with OpenFeature
You have not chosen a provider yet and just need boolean toggles — OpenFeature alone does not store or serve flags
A simple env-based toggle is enough and provider wiring is overhead
Your chosen vendor's native SDK is required for advanced features not exposed via its OpenFeature provider
You are prototyping quickly and vendor neutrality is not a near-term concern
